title: Existence and sectionwise uniqueness of completed pullback tensor evaluation
statement: For a scheme morphism f : X ⟶ Y, level n, and sequence coefficient map ρ equal to the canonical constant-section map integralComparisonSequenceRingMap [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], direct image along ρ followed by level-n evaluation [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] is naturally isomorphic to level-n evaluation followed by canonical coefficient direct image. The comparison acts as the identity on every section. For any ρ, any two comparisons satisfying this sectionwise identity are equal.

source.place: Tags 03D1 and 0941, sectionwise direct image and evaluation comparison

proof.text: Substitute the canonical sequence coefficient map for ρ. Write a and b for the ring identifications of level-n evaluation on Y and X. The two site functor composites are definitionally equal. The composite ring maps agree: the components of a and b are identity ring homomorphisms, and the component of integralComparisonSequenceRingMap at (n,U) is definitionally coefficientProEtaleDirectRingMap at U. Apply Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardComp to both composites and connect them by pushforwardCongr for this equality. Each of these comparisons acts as the identity on sections, so their composite does too. The private sectionwiseIdentity_trans lemma combines the three heterogeneous identity formulas using transitivity; the component identities are the existing Mathlib pushforward comparison lemmas. The common composite site functor and source ring are supplied explicitly to pushforwardCongr to fix the intended factorization.

For uniqueness with arbitrary ρ, apply Iso.ext, NatTrans.ext, SheafOfModules.hom_ext and sectionwise extensionality. Transitivity of the two heterogeneous identity formulas gives equality of the underlying section maps.

statement_change.old_statement: For a scheme morphism f : X ⟶ Y and level n, the direct image on coefficient sequences followed by level-n evaluation is naturally isomorphic to level-n evaluation followed by coefficient direct image. The comparison acts as the identity on every section; any two such comparisons with this sectionwise identity are equal.
statement_change.what: The former Lean existence statement allowed an arbitrary coefficient map ρ. The identity between the two underlying abelian section objects need not be linear for a twisted ρ. For f = id and an unramified quadratic coefficient extension, residue Frobenius gives such a twist on the regular module. Require equality with the canonical constant-section map, as already intended by the node and used by its sole consumer. Uniqueness remains valid for arbitrary ρ.

old_proof.text: Construct the comparison on the underlying sheaves by the identity on sections. The restriction-of-scalars coefficient action does not change the underlying section map, so the identity is natural and satisfies the displayed section formula. Sheaf and module extensionality show that a comparison with this formula is unique.
